title: Can we draw a complete picture of a line?
description: A straight piece with end points A and B is stretched beyond A on one side and beyond B on the other, and the stretching never stops. Only a part of it fits on the paper, so arrowheads show that it continues. Keeko's doubt, that a line has two end points, is broken by the stretched mark that has no dot at either side.
teaching_notes: One idea: a line goes on forever in both directions, so only a part of it can be drawn. Watch for students who think that a line has end points like a line segment.

source: Imagine that the line segment AB is extended beyond A in one d
video_script.why: The child sees that stretching a line segment without any end gives a line, and that a line cannot be drawn completely on paper.
video_script.substitution: Stretch the segment beyond both end points and watch it leave the page.
video_script.anchor: the line segment AB stretched beyond A on one side and beyond B on the other side, on a sheet of paper
video_script.wrong_answer: a line has two end points
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a line has two end points because the line segment had them. The stretched mark has no dot at either side, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: No, a line goes on forever in both directions

final_answer.value: No; a line goes on forever in both directions, so only a part of it can be drawn, with arrowheads
final_answer.spoken: no, a line goes on forever in both directions, so we draw only a part of it

never_show: arrowheads on the stretched mark before the answer beat
maths_rules: The line segment AB has two end points, A and B.
Stretching it beyond A in one direction and beyond B in the other direction without any end gives a line.
A line has no end point on either side, so it goes on forever in both directions.
A sheet of paper has edges, so only a part of a line can be drawn, and arrowheads show that it continues.
Slip: a line has no end points; only a line segment has two.
video_script.design: One idea: a line has no end, so we cannot draw all of it. The line segment AB stays on the board and is stretched on both sides. The wrong idea is that a line has two end points.
